product_results.title: Nitecore NU25 360 Lumen Triple Output - White, Red, High CRI - Lightweight USB Rechargeable Headlamp (Black)

about_item: 360 LUMEN WIDE BEAM - Featuring a CREE XP-G2 S3 LED for a primary output, the NU25 is capable of 360 lumen max output and 88 yards of throw, perfect for biking, jogging and trekking.

AUXILIARY HIGH CRI AND RED LED LIGHTS - The high CRI auxiliary light produces richer more natural looking colors over standard LEDs making it a great tool for up close tasks requiring fine detail while the auxiliary red LED is great for preserving night vision.
COMPACT AND LIGHTWEIGHT - Weighing less than an ounce (0.99oz w/o headband, 1.9oz w/ headband) and small enough to fit in a pocket, the NU25 is comfortable for daily use and long excursions.

NO CHARGER NEEDED - The headlamp is great for travel and daily use because it uses a built-in micro-USB battery can easily be charged on-the-go using a micro-USB charging cable connected to any USB power source.
PACKAGE CONTENTS - NITECORE NU25 (This is the 2017 version), Headband, USB-Micro USB Charging Cable, LumenTac wall charging adapter

authors_reviews.title: Small and Mighty
authors_reviews.text: Backpacker here. I look for light weight, effective, an ability to solve several problems, and for battery operated items - long life, quick charging, and low mAh. We have multiple tools to keep charged so nothing that goes in my pack or on my body can be power greedy.This is my second Nitecore NU25. I found myself using my first one so much - both on and off the trail - that I bought a second one for my hiking partner.Safe to say I’m a fan.The red light lowest setting is perfect for tent activities. I’ve hiked into the night hours with that same setting, but find that the second power setting give me a better picture on unfamiliar trails. I can pick up rocks and roots, keep from getting my eye poked out with a branch, and avoid nighttime spider webs that always seem perfectly set up to catch unsuspecting hikers in the face. Orb weaver anyone?I know we shouldn’t be hiking around at night, but it happens sometimes. This light has gotten me out of some nighttime jams.It excels for use around camp and anywhere else you want a headlamp. I don’t need solar flare strength lights for most of what we do. The options in this light are just right for everything that needs doing.The battery life seems ample - as I’ve never run it out to zero. It charges surprisingly fast and is good to go quickly. I think it sips about 300 mAh, leaving plenty for other items.The light can be removed from its strap and sewed directly into your favorite wool cap for lighter cool weather trekking.The strap on my first one has stretched a bit over these last could of years, but I can still snug it up when I need to.I’ve avoided rechargeable lights in the past because I just preferred to carry a few extra batteries, but this light changed my mind of light that. It’s been reliable and a good tool for managing the moon side of the world.
authors_reviews.author: David D

authors_reviews.title: fantastic controls
authors_reviews.text: The headlamp does exactly what you want (provide light) and has reduced all the stuff you don't (having to think about it).The controls are excellent;-Positive clicks with sufficient tension on the lamp tilt, without being loud or requiring excessive effort.-Separate buttons for red and white LED light, no confusion about what will come on.-The lamps starts on the dimmest setting for both lamp colors, reduces accidentally blinding yourself.-You don't have to click up through the brighter settings to get it to turn off!! This is really the best part.I don't particularly care about the weight of the unit. For those who do - while the lamp itself is very light weight, the head band (which is wonderful, comfy and stays put) roughly doubles the carry weight and probably triples the carry volume.I likely will not replace the strap until it fails (which I don't expect to happen for some time) I may remove some of the extra adjustment length.I find the spread and throw distance of the high beam to be sufficient for night hiking/walking/jogging, (carrying it at waist level greatly increases the visual relief of tripping hazards) and generally keep it much dimmer if just working around camp or using it for field work, but it will not replace a tighter beamed flashlight for distance illumination or faster travel (like biking).Overall an excellent headlamp that does everything I expect a headlamp to do, and doesn't do anything to annoy me while in use.
authors_reviews.author: Laird

authors_reviews.title: Great headlamp for running. Not the brightest but is lightweight and rechargeable
authors_reviews.text: This is a great head lamp for what I imagine would be a variety of activities in the dark. For context, I was looking for a head lamp specifically for when I go out running in the afternoons. Because I run in my neighborhood, I didn’t need something super bright but something bright enough for me to be able to not trip and ensure cars could see me when I cross the street. For that purpose, this light achieved what I wanted and even exceeded expectations with the night vision options, light tilting ability, and the fact that it is rechargeable which was a huge factor for me. Since buying this in early November I have only had to charge it once and it is now mid December and I use this thing weekly on my runs. Very happy with how long the charge lasts. The weight is fantastic as I was worried about running with a brick on my head but this is not the case with this product and I barely notice it is there. The night vision options are great and really enjoy the flashing red option in the early afternoons when it’s not very dark out as it gives me options for how I want to be visible by cars without buying a bunch of different lights. I usually use the second most bright setting for the white light. The dimmest setting seems useless on runs and the super bright setting is nice but found it can drain the battery quickly. Overall very happy and have enjoyed this purchase.
authors_reviews.author: Kyle

authors_reviews.title: Lightweight, rugged, reliable!
authors_reviews.text: Wow - these little lights are incredible! I've used this unit for more than a month worth of camping, hiking and general outdoor activity. It's light enough that I forget that I'm wearing it, bright enough to see everything I need to (and everything else with the TURBO mode), and with enough of a battery that it gets me through the night without worry of it going dead.I bought the NU25 based on reviews from other hikers who were searching for lightweight options for backpacking, and haven't been disappointed! That being said, this is a SMALL headlamp (US quarter in pictures for size comparison), so it wouldn't be difficult to misplace if you're inclined to have things just laying about. The battery capacity is more than enough for me to go several evenings of use, but I also use the lower power settings unless the situation really calls for a very bright light.Now for the pros/cons:Pros:-Ultralight, the head strap weighs just as much as the light itself.-Easily rechargeable with the included micro-usb cable.-Both white and red LED options.-Multiple power options for both red and white LED's.-Quick to recharge and plenty of power!-Comfortable to wear, no worries about slipping off or pressing into your forehead too much.Cons:-Not as cheap as easily accessible headlamps (but you get what you pay for!)-Comparably dim to most entry-level headlamps (but more than enough if you're comfortable only seeing everything within 80 feet, instead of 500 feet!).In conclusion, an excellent choice if you're needing a lightweight headlamp for any outdoor activities, visibility while running, or just to keep around for emergencies!
authors_reviews.author: Truitt in the Trees

authors_reviews.title: Excellent balance of characteristics; very useable in colder weather
authors_reviews.text: This is a great little headlamp. It’s lightweight, retains functionality for a long time at low battery levels, is very useable in colder temperatures if you do it correctly, is low enough profile to sleep with on your head, is not overly complex like most headlamps, is plenty bright for hiking around in the dark. I’ve used in successfully in fairly cold conditions (lows in teens and twenties, highs in 30s, long nights in northern latitudes). I keep it on me most of the time including wearing it in sleeping bag. When you do that, battery life is good notwithstanding a lot of low temp criticisms I’ve read. Just like all battery powered electronics in the backcountry, gotta do a little to keep them warm if you can.
authors_reviews.author: BGH

authors_reviews.title: Solid headlamp, lackluster brightness settings. Please give me a red spotlight!
authors_reviews.text: I bought two of these for my partner and I and we used them for our entire '21 AT thru hike. A year later I still got ~9 hours of the mid-intensity white light in ~freezing weather.The good:-Charges quickly, and can be used while plugged in. I forgot to charge mine and was able to run it off a battery bank in a shoulder strap pocket with the USB plugged in, which was a bit awkward in my face but beats hiking in the dark.-Ultralight, except the way-too-big band. The headlamp is 1.1oz, the band is 0.9 oz. I took the band off and use a single piece of shock cord with a linelock. It's light enough it's still very comfortable, I don't sweat as much, and I wore it around my neck full-time with the short days to keep the battery warm. The original band is pretty bulky to try that.-Good brightness at white/medium--comfortable to hike at. I found the Princetontek Byte as my second pick too dim for tough terrain.-Has a red feature. If you do any stargazing or want to do basic tasks in camp after dark, or are going to be around other hikers a lot, using red is a universal courtesy. Rolling into camp at midnight and flashing peoples tents with white lights is not cool!The bad:-You don't need a massive band for a 1.1oz headlight. Ditch the band and carry a full blown spare?-The light intensity options aren't good. White/low is too dark to hike by, white/high kills the battery too fast and is pretty blinding. The high-CRI and turbo modes are basically useless battery killers, and I've swapped to them two or three times ever. The white/mid and red lights are basically the only useful options here, and I really want something between white low/mid instead.-The red light is "flood" only. Nitecore: PLEASE GIVE ME A RED SPOTLIGHT. Because it's super floody, even red-high isn't bright enough to hike by--if it was a spot lens, this would be my ideal headlamp.-Red "flood" means it still gets in everybody's eyes. Sure, it's lower intensity and doesn't wreck your night vision, but sitting around camp eating it gets really annoying that the red light is spilling everywhere instead of just where the person using it wants to lookI can't complain too much because this is still my go-to headlamp. I checked out the 2022 model and would still buy the older model, it looks like Nitecore actually made most of these problems worse with the update (bizarre brightness settings that make poor use of battery life, lots of over-spilling floodlights, and an even worse red).If Nitecore made this headlamp with customizable or adjustable brightness settings and a red spotlight, I don't see how any other design could compete and I'd buy it in a heartbeat. *NUDGE NUDGE*
authors_reviews.author: Erik

authors_reviews.title: Best light
authors_reviews.text: For years I have loved this headlamp and thought it was the most superior one out there. I have sung it's praises offline and recommended or even bought it for my friends.BUT, I just accidentally had it go through the laundry on heavy wash cycle, and it still somehow works PERFECTLY, and that pretty much seals the deal, so I decided to write a review (*Note: Don't try this at home*)This headlamp has it all. It is incredibly lightweight and the light lasts forever, particularly the red light option. I hiked the PCT with it, and it pretty much never ran out of battery for me. I'd just randomly recharge it when I felt like it had been a while. But my favorite part is the separate red light and white light buttons. It is so much better at night to be able to immediately choose the red light option without first ruining your night vision (or that of others) by having to click through the white button first. I love the control that this light weight head lamp gives me.Best of all, it has so many more features than other headlamps while not being any more expensive.Highly recommend!
authors_reviews.author: Kristina Geddert

authors_reviews.title: Excellent ultralight headlamp option!
authors_reviews.text: I still need to do long-term field testing of this headlamp, but so far I'm super impressed. My previous headlamp was the Black Diamond ReVolt rechargeable lamp, but I always thought it was bulky, heavy, and not that bright when night hiking.The Nitecore is bright, light weight, and because it's so compact it is less likely to bob or bounce on the head. I also like that it has a dedicated button for the red light and I'm less likely to get lost in the various modes selections.So far the only theoretical strike against it is that the battery isn't field replaceable. The benefit of something like the ReVolt is that it can use generic AAA batteries. But that said, as more of my kit is dependent on carrying a USB rechargeable battery pack, I'm getting more comfortable with with that as a core component of my backcountry system. If I'm solo hiking or in a very remote area, I always have a backup plan in case I have a total electronics failure.Also, for the gram counters out there, there are some good youtube videos on replacing the headband with bungee cord to make it even lighter. Personally, I prefer a more robust headband for comfort and stability. Also, the included headband feels high quality - soft against the skin.
